title: Malawi
capsule: Malawi became an independent republic on 6 July 1964, having been the British protectorate of Nyasaland since 1891, with Hastings Banda becoming the country's first prime minister and subsequently life president from 1966 until 1994. Banda's three-decade rule was characterized by one-party governance under the Malawi Congress Party, strict censorship, and forced labor policies alongside relative economic stability from tobacco and tea exports. Following a 1993 referendum that mandated multiparty democracy, Bakili Muluzi defeated Banda in the 1994 elections, inaugurating a democratic transition that has continued despite persistent poverty rankings placing Malawi among the world's least-developed economies.
